title: Mathematical and computational roots
description: Build intuition for probability, computation, information, and trainable units.

title: Symbolic AI and early language systems
description: See how early AI represented facts, searched for solutions, and handled language.

title: Statistical learning
description: Compare instance methods, clustering, likelihood, learnability, margins, ensembles, and optimization.

title: Neural networks to deep learning
description: Trace representations from recurrent and energy-based networks to modern deep training.

title: NLP and language modeling
description: Follow statistical translation and word representations into attention and pretrained Transformers.

title: Knowledge graphs and neuro-symbolic AI
description: Learn where graph facts come from, how links are learned, and how rules connect to neural models.

title: Reinforcement learning
description: Move from value prediction to policy gradients, deep control, self-play, and planning.

title: Vision and multimodal learning
description: Follow CNNs through visual self-supervision, Transformers, image-language models, and generation.

title: LLMs, instruction tuning, and reasoning
description: Understand pretraining, scaling, retrieval, alignment, adaptation, and reasoning.

title: AI for science and current directions
description: Apply graph and sequence models to chemistry, proteins, materials, and genomics.

title: Tool use and autonomous agents
description: Study how language models browse, plan, use tools, remember earlier work, and act in interactive environments. Read the benchmarks alongside the systems they evaluate.
